t: 2032 — First long-duration hazard handling testbed runs a sealed yard h
title: 2032 — First long-duration hazard handling testbed runs a sealed yard h
definition: 2032 milestone on the Starship Recycling Yards roadmap.
description:
First long-duration hazard handling testbed runs a sealed yard hulls habitat for 1,000 days on Earth, proving the cutting docks recycling math.

What must be true first: the cutting docks results have to replicate outside the lab, yard logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and material recovery operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed cutting docks demonstrations, yard logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting material recovery uptime. When all three flash green, 2032 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (6 years from the 2026 baseline.)

definition: Estimates Starship Recycling Yards readiness from component maturity.

title: Starship Recycling Yards Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Starship Recycling Yards operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Starship Recycling Yards installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 12879 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where cutting docks monitoring, yard logistics redundancy, or material recovery maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Starship Recycling Yards Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Starship Recycling Yards: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Starship Recycling Yards — yards dismantling retired starships into new hulls.

Phase 1 — Prove (cutting docks): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (yard logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (material recovery): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (hazard handling): yard hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and outer system-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
